stem: A postoperative client with an abdominal incision is taking shallow breaths and is reluctant to cough because movement worsens incisional pain. Which nursing intervention best addresses this barrier while supporting pulmonary hygiene?

options.A: Use prescribed pain-control measures as appropriate, teach the client to splint the incision, and coach deep breathing and coughing.
options.B: Have the client perform deep breathing and coughing before pain treatment so respiratory findings are not affected by analgesia.
options.C: Assist with early ambulation and defer coached coughing and deep breathing because both interventions address postoperative ventilation.
options.D: Encourage leg exercises and repositioning before addressing the painful shallow breathing because they also prevent postoperative complications.

rationale: Postoperative respiratory care includes coached deep breathing and coughing, incision splinting, and early ambulation to support ventilation and secretion clearance. In this client, incisional pain is the stated barrier to effective pulmonary hygiene, so appropriate prescribed pain-control measures plus splinting directly address that barrier and support participation in coughing and deep breathing. Early ambulation complements these measures but does not justify deferring targeted pulmonary-hygiene exercises. Leg exercises primarily address venous-stasis prevention and do not correct the client's pain-limited shallow breathing.
educational_objective: When incisional pain limits postoperative coughing and deep breathing, combine appropriate prescribed pain control with incision splinting and coached pulmonary-hygiene exercises; early ambulation is complementary rather than a substitute for targeted airway-clearance and lung-expansion measures.
source_organization: Open Resources for Nursing (Open RN) / Chippewa Valley Technical College; hosted by NCBI Bookshelf
source_locator: Chapter 2 Perioperative Care > postoperative procedures, Prevention of Respiratory Complications: breathing exercises/incentive spirometry promote lung expansion and help prevent atelectasis; coughing and splinting are taught for secretion clearance. Section 2.5, Table 2.5b Routine Postoperative Nursing Interventions: teach coughing/deep breathing or prescribed incentive spirometry, teach splinting of the surgical area, assist early ambulation to promote ventilation and secretion removal, and manage pain with prescribed pharmacological and nonpharmacological strategies.
source_claim_supported: Postoperative pulmonary hygiene includes deep breathing/coughing, incision splinting, and early ambulation, while prescribed pain-management strategies support postoperative care when pain limits participation.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Appendix A, Physiological Adaptation, p. 46: Provide postoperative care; Provide pulmonary hygiene (e.g., chest physiotherapy, incentive spirometry); Manage the care of a client with impaired ventilation/oxygenation; Recognize signs and symptoms of client complications and intervene.
correction_summary: Rebuilt the item to remove the uniquely-long keyed answer and obvious distractors, made incisional pain an explicit barrier to pulmonary hygiene, balanced clinically relevant alternatives, and remapped the primary NCLEX client need to Physiological Adaptation because the construct is postoperative pulmonary-hygiene management.

audit_findings.clinical_category: Postoperative pulmonary hygiene with pain-limited coughing/deep breathing
audit_findings.stem: PASS — realistic abdominal-postoperative scenario with the barrier to pulmonary hygiene stated explicitly.
audit_findings.option_A: PASS — directly addresses the pain barrier and uses source-supported splinting plus coughing/deep breathing; uniquely best.
audit_findings.option_B: PASS as distractor — pulmonary-hygiene exercises are appropriate, but deliberately placing them before needed pain management fails to address the stated barrier.
audit_findings.option_C: PASS as distractor — early ambulation is beneficial and source-supported, but it complements rather than replaces or delays targeted coughing/deep-breathing measures in this scenario.
audit_findings.option_D: PASS as distractor — leg exercises/repositioning have postoperative roles but do not directly address the client's pain-limited shallow breathing and secretion-clearance needs.
audit_findings.ambiguity: PASS — A is the only option that directly resolves the stated barrier while preserving the recommended pulmonary-hygiene interventions.
audit_findings.second_answer: EXCLUDED — C contains a beneficial component but is rendered inferior by deferring the targeted intervention; B and D do not appropriately address the barrier.
audit_findings.cueing: PASS — the keyed answer is not the longest, option lengths are comparable, and no absolute-word pattern identifies the key.
audit_findings.blueprint: PASS — NCSBN Physiological Adaptation directly includes postoperative care and pulmonary hygiene.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: PASS — challenged whether early ambulation alone could be equally correct; because the stem specifies pain-limited coughing/shallow breathing, the option that treats the barrier and supports splinting plus coached pulmonary hygiene remains uniquely best.
